# Expert read: Lean proof engineering (2026-11-03)

Slug `lean-proof-engineering`. The persona: maintains a large Lean 4 library, reviews Mathlib PRs,
has been through a module-system migration. Reads statements, not names; treats `decide +kernel` on
a fixture as a test; treats `native_decide`/`bv_decide` as compiled trust; counts what `@[expose]`
costs at rebuild; asks of every "census" and "tooth" whether it can fail.

Tags: **READ** (file opened, `path:line` as of the working tree on 2026-11-03), **INFERRED**
(deduced from READ facts), **PROPOSED**. Every number has its command. I edited nothing but this
file and ran no build. Paths below are relative to `/Users/ember/dev/obend/lean/` unless they start
with `review/` or are a root document.

Read first: `review/FABLE-COUNCIL-20261101.md` §1–§2. I extend it; where the working tree has moved
since (it has: 480 modules, 234K lines, `find Obend -name '*.lean' | xargs wc -l`), I say so.

---

## 0. Verdict in one paragraph

**INFERRED.** The *mechanism* (`#tooth`, `#assert_axioms_tree`, `#assert_compiled`, the two tiers)
is better than most Lean projects have, and the median theorem in the tree is real: a uniform
sample of thirty gives 21 universally quantified statements with content. The failure is at the
*headline*: 66 of the 68 `golden_*`/`*_verified` theorems are closed instances; the 32 `X.accepted
= true` conjuncts in `Obend/Apps` are `true = true` by construction; the "silicon kernel" that is
lowered is a type-code comparator with fixture-fitted special cases on the host side; 176 bare
identifiers cited in the root documents name no declaration, and the documents census that is
supposed to catch that only looks at `Obend.`-prefixed tokens, so it passes. The gate's two real
holes are (a) nothing distinguishes a fixture from a theorem anywhere the numbers are reported, and
(b) tier 2 (census, teeth, Apps) is manual: 87 sources are newer than the last `Census.olean`, four
of eight `Apps` modules have never been built in this tree, and 30 test files with 308 theorems and
157 `#tooth` commands belong to no build target. The rebuild cascade is the same disease from the
other side: fixture proofs by `decide +kernel` across modules force `@[expose] public section` on
39 of 43 Hardware files, and a one-line exposed edit in `Core/Term.lean` now reaches 333 of 439
tier-1 modules.

---

## 1. Suspicions, evidence, verdicts (ranked by how it would read to a Lean maintainer)

| # | Suspicion | What would clear it | Found | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "0 sorryAx, N theorems" headlines count fixtures as theorems | A census line that separates closed statements from universal ones | No such line exists; `#assert_axioms_tree` counts constants only (`Obend/AssertAxioms.lean:58-80`) | **Confirmed** (§3, §4) |
| 2 | `X.accepted = true` is vacuous | `accepted` defined from a checker result | `#import_obend` emits `@[expose] public def Ns.accepted : Bool := true` and `theorem Ns.accepted_eq : Ns.accepted = true := rfl` (`Obend/Apps/ObendRisc.lean:621-624`; same text in the other seven Apps; `Obend/Elab/Workbook.lean:1713-1719`) | **Confirmed**: the information is "the macro did not throw" |
| 3 | The "Lean kernel checker" lowered to silicon is not a kernel | A `KExpr`-consuming `LExpr`/`Book` | `kernelCheckLExpr` is a three-`Nat` comparator (`Obend/Lower/LeanKernel.lean:1058-1073`); `encodeDeclCheckLExpr` runs `kernelCheckDecl` on the host to produce `inferredTag` (`:1080-1092`); the newer `inferTypeLExpr` is a 4-word type-code table with host-side fixture patches (§5.2) | **Confirmed**, and worse than the council found |

## 2. The mechanism, file by file (READ)

### 2.1 `Obend/Tactic/Tooth.lean` (294 lines)

Lines 1–226 are the real thing: `#tooth T by mutation f := v` walks the dependency graph of the
*stored* proof of `T` by compiled constant collection (`:22-45`), refuses hidden bodies, cyclic
replacement, unsafe/partial defs, inductives in the affected set (`:140-156`), replays the renamed
original closure as a control (`:196-203`), then replays under the mutation through `addDeclCore`
with `doCheck := true` (`:181-186`) and credits a tooth only on a kernel type-mismatch class of
exception (`:160-166`). It errors when the stored proof still succeeds (`:224`). That is a correct
mutation test and it is the best piece of tooling in the repository.

Lines 228–294 (added in `23a7651`, 2026-11-02, uncommitted diff is empty) bolt on a "Dual-Pole
Tooth Obligation Checker": `verifyDualPoleTooth spec := spec.eval spec.posFixture && spec.negFixtures.all
(fun x => !spec.eval x)` and `verifyDualPoleTooth_sound`, whose conclusion is the definition
unfolded. It is used only in `tests/metasystem/IsarJudgeAndWorkspaceTest.lean` (17 uses; `grep -rn
verifyDualPoleTooth Obend tests`), which nothing builds. **INFERRED**: a fixture checker was given
the name of the mutation tester so that "tooth" counts could rise. It should leave this file.

### 2.2 `Obend/AssertAxioms.lean`, `Obend/AssertCompiled.lean`

`#assert_axioms_tree` (`AssertAxioms.lean:58-80`) iterates `env.constants.map₁`, filters to package
modules, refuses any axiom not `_native`-suffixed and any constant whose axiom closure leaves
{`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`} except via `_native` (counted) or a `computed_fields`
`_override` with `lcProof` (counted). `#assert_compiled` (`AssertCompiled.lean:36-88`) re-runs the
oracle's closed `Bool` claim through `evalExpr` and refuses by-name acceptance. Both are sound for
what they claim. What they do not claim: anything about the *shape* of a theorem. A closed
`decide +kernel` fixture is as kernel-clean as `lower_sound`; the census cannot tell them apart,
and the documents quote its verdict line as if it could (`METATHEORY.md:4-7`).

Not a `module` (so it sees private parts and the legacy leaves; `:10-15`); imports every file; a
`run_cmd` walks `Obend/` and refuses an unimported file or a module in neither tier's globs
(`:471-520`, parsing `lakefile.toml` by string splitting); then `#assert_axioms_tree` and
`#docs_census`. It is tier 2 (`lakefile.toml:33-35`), built by hand (`tools/hooks/pre-push:2-5`).

## 4. The `accepted = true` pattern (READ)

`grep -rnE 'accepted = true' Obend/Apps | wc -l` = 32 conjunct sites in 8 files. Each `accepted` is
emitted by a local `#import_obend` elaborator (`Apps/ObendRisc.lean:612-651`, duplicated per app)
that runs `elaborateRiscObendFile` at compile time, throws on `.error`, and on `.ok` emits
`@[expose] public def Ns.accepted : Bool := true` and `public theorem Ns.accepted_eq : Ns.accepted = true := rfl`
(`:621-624`). `WorkbookPackage.accepted` is set `:= true` at `Elab/Workbook.lean:533` and `:1570`
after `FrontEnd.accept` succeeded. The *elaboration succeeding* is a real build-time test; the
*theorem* carries no information. By contrast the per-claim `claim_*_holds` theorems the same macro
emits (`ObendRisc.lean:641-650`) are the right shape: statement `obligationMeaningWithJudges … obj just`,
proof `obligationWithJudges_sound` applied to a `decide +kernel` on the checker — a kernel-checked
instance *with a semantic meaning*. The honest version of the 32 conjuncts is to delete them and
let the `_holds` theorems stand.

Hardware 39/43, Lower 22/25, Vault 14/16, Consensus 4/4, Logic 9/9, Equiv 10/13, Core 56/150,
Spec 2/29, Slot 0/9, Run 1/26. `Core/Term.lean` itself is `public section` with per-def
`@[expose]` (`:9,15,20,…`), i.e. the hub is disciplined; the leaves are not.

**PROPOSED estimate for the same Term edit now.** Lines in the closure grew 2.3×, modules 1.5×.
Linear in lines, Σ per-module time ≈ 800 s; at two threads with the Core→Lower→Hardware→Analysis
chain as critical path, **8–12 minutes wall on an idle Mac**, and the new Hardware/Apps modules are
heavier per line than Core (169 `decide +kernel` in Hardware; `SiliconElabFabric.lean` 3190 lines,
`LeanKernel.lean` 2420) so **10–20 minutes is the range I would bet on**, 3–6× the 2026-11-01
figure; under today's load 45 it will not finish in the hook's patience. On hbox with
`swarm-build` and more threads, 3–6 minutes. The honest number is the one `tools/measure.sh` prints
when rerun on hbox; nobody has run it since 283 jobs. Note also that `measure.sh` measures the
*rarest* dangerous edit (appending to Term); the common one is a body edit inside a blanket-exposed
Hardware file, which rebuilds that file's dependents even when no importer reduces it.

**INFERRED, the connection:** waves 5–6 proved by `decide +kernel` *across modules* on fixture
data; that requires the definitions to be `@[expose]`d for the importer's kernel to reduce them;
the lanes therefore wrote `@[expose] public section` at the top of every file. The fixture proof
style and the rebuild cascade are one decision.

---

## 8. What I would change about the gate so the pattern cannot recur (PROPOSED)

1. **A statement-shape census next to the axiom census.** A `#theorem_census` in
   `Obend/AssertAxioms.lean` style: for every package `thmInfo`, strip `let`s, and call the
   statement *closed* if it has no `forallE` binder whose domain is not a `Prop` or an instance.
   Print per-module counts `theorems / closed`; refuse a closed statement that is not declared
   through a `fixture` command (a thin wrapper that adds an attribute), and refuse a `theorem` whose
   name ends in `_sound`/`_complete`/`_verified`/`golden_*` while its statement is closed. Docs may
   quote only the two census verdict lines. ~200 lines; one lane-day; the migration of ~700
   declarations is mechanical (`sed` on the keyword) and the number the headline loses is the
   number that was never a theorem.
2. **Tier 2 cannot be stale.** The pre-push hook refuses when `Census.olean` is older than any
   source or any `Apps` module lacks an olean, and prints the hbox command. Add
   `tests/metasystem`, `tests/silicon_elab`, `tests/rehydration` to a `Tests` lib or delete them;
   308 theorems that nothing elaborates are prose. ~30 lines of shell, one lakefile stanza.
3. **Bare-name resolution in `#docs_census`.** Extract every backticked `[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(_[A-Za-z0-9]+)+`
   token, resolve by suffix against `env.constants`, fail on dangling. 40 lines in
   `DocsCensus.lean`; the real cost is rewriting 113 citations in the seven governed docs, which is
   the point. Invoke `#check_docs_census` too, or delete it.
4. **Exposure is per-def, never per-file, outside `Core`.** The census `run_cmd` already reads
   files; add a check that `@[expose] public section` appears only under an allow-list
   (`Core/Term`, `Core/Ty`, `Core/Data`, codecs). Migrate Hardware first (39 files). One lane-day
   per directory; the measurement in §7 is the control.
5. **`#tooth` refuses closed targets** (same closedness test as 1): a tooth on a fixture only
   proves the fixture is sensitive. 10 lines beside `Tooth.lean:175`. Move `verifyDualPoleTooth`
   out of `Tooth.lean`.
6. **One `#import_obend`.** The macro is copied as `local elab` into seven Apps files and
   `Hardware/UserspacePhysical.lean:798` (`grep -rn 'elab "#import_obend' Obend`); Workbook already owns
   it (`Workbook.lean:1777`). Delete the copies; drop `accepted_eq`.

---

## 9. Three changes first, with cost, and one question

1. **Fixture keyword + shape census (8.1).** Cost: one agent-day for the command, one for the
   mechanical migration, a tier-2 build on hbox to confirm. Benefit: every number in `METATHEORY.md`
   becomes checkable and the 66/68 and 32/32 patterns cannot be written again without the build
   saying so.
2. **Tier-2 freshness gate + tests as a target (8.2).** Cost: half a day plus the first honest
   tier-2 run on hbox, which will surface whatever the four never-built Apps and the 87 changed
   files have broken. Benefit: "0 sorryAx" means the tree in front of you.
3. **Bare-name docs census + Hardware de-blanketing (8.3, 8.4).** Cost: two agent-days of edits,
   mostly prose, plus one `measure.sh` run on hbox before and after. Benefit: the documents stop
   describing a different system, and the one-edit cost comes back under what the hook can carry.

**The question for Ember:** when the census starts printing `theorems / fixtures` separately,
are you willing for the headline to read something like *7,100 theorems, 700 fixtures* instead of
*7,861 theorems* — i.e. is the number allowed to go down, or must the fixtures keep the keyword?
Everything in §8 follows from that answer.

atoms.t: # Sitting next to the physicist: validated numerics, multiphysics, motor drives, photonics (2026-11-03)
Slug `physics-numerics`. The persona: validated numerics (intervals, Taylor models, verified ODE
enclosures), finite-element magnetics, motor-drive and power-electronics design, with photonics and
quantum-hardware colleagues. Working tree as of 2026-11-03, not HEAD; nothing edited but this file.
Tags: **READ** (file opened, `path:line` cited), **INFERRED** (deduced from READ facts), **PROPOSED**.
Every number has the command or the arithmetic that produced it. No Lean or Rust was built. Runs:
`verilator --lint-only -Wall` on one `.sv`; `lean/.lake/build/bin/obend check|run|prove` on a scratch
module in the session scratchpad; `grep`/`wc`.
Files read in full or by theorem statement: `lean/Obend/Analysis/{RealAnalysis,TaylorModel,Flowpipe,
Hybrid,Diff,Groebner,SosLyapunov,Equitable,QuantumWalk,EqSatHypergraph}.lean`,
`lean/Obend/Judge/RealAnalysis.lean`, `lean/Obend/Elab/AutoCert.lean`, `lean/Obend/Hardware/{Magnetics,
FluidThermal,PowerElectronics,Thermal,Physics,Photonics,QuantumMatter,Analog,RF,DSP,Accelerators,
FabuBlox,TcadBridge,DigitalTwin}.lean`, `lean/Obend/Apps/{FocHil,SdrFt8,QuantumPhotonicMatter}.lean`,
`apps/foc-hil/**`, `apps/sdr-ft8/verilator/*`, `apps/quantum-photonic-matter/verilator/*_tb.cpp`,
`stdlib/physical/*.obend`, `PHYSICAL.md` (30,403 lines by `wc -l` over the list in the brief).
## 0. Verdict
**READ/INFERRED.** The arithmetic core is now genuinely verified and the council's "zero theorems in
`RealAnalysis.lean`" finding is obsolete in the working tree: `Interval.add_mem/sub_mem/mul_mem/sqr_mem`,
`evalInterval_sound`, three `#tooth` probes (`RealAnalysis.lean:184-307,402-464,471-499`), the Taylor-model
algebra (`TaylorModel.add_models/sub_models/scale_models/mul_models`, `evalTaylorModelRange_encloses`,
`TaylorModel.lean:451-713`), forward-mode interval AD (`Diff.lean:313`), the SOS/Positivstellensatz
family (`Judge/RealAnalysis.lean:943`, `SosLyapunov.lean:413,501,672`) and the interval judge
(`Judge/RealAnalysis.lean:83-119`) are universally quantified over `ℚ` and their proofs are structural.
A numerical analyst would sign those pages.
Everything that *names a device* sits on top of that core without touching it. Physical constants enter
as integer literals inside `def golden…` records and `decide +kernel` theorems; no theorem has a device
parameter as a free variable whose *value* matters, and in the two places a model enters as a hypothesis
(`AnalyticModel`, `TaylorModel.lean:935`; `perturbative_disorder_leakage_bound`, `QuantumMatter.lean:1786`)
the only instance is a polynomial or the hypothesis is the conclusion's own recurrence. The FOC
"closed loop" is open in Lean (the sensor is never updated) and plant-free in the HIL (no inverter, no
mechanics, thermal state moves 0.4 K in the whole run). The automatic certificate synthesizer certifies a
claim over a domain it chose, not the domain the claim states. Three of the four golden "multiphysics"
numbers are unit mismatches a motor-drive engineer would catch in the first minute.
The referee's one-line summary: *correct interval arithmetic over the rationals, wearing the names of
machines it has never been connected to.*
## 1. Where does any physical constant or device parameter enter a theorem?
I asked this first of every module. The table is exhaustive for the files in the brief.
| Module | How a parameter enters | Is it a hypothesis a proof depends on? |

| `TaylorModel.lean` | Lagrange constants `1/40, 1/720, 1/120, 32/5, 5/8` typed into `lagrangeRem*` (`:200-221`); validity domains `[-1,1]`, `[-1/2,1/2]` (`:717-734`) | Only via `AnalyticModel` (`:935-970`), whose single instance (`:976`) defines `expFn := expPartialSum 8`, `sinFn := sinDegree7Odd`, etc. **READ**: `grep -rn AnalyticModel lean/Obend --include='*.lean' \| grep -v TaylorModel.lean` is empty. No consumer. |

| `Flowpipe.lean` | `OdeSystem.remainderPad : Interval := ofPoint 0` (`:44`); concrete pads `[-1/10,1/10]` (`:308`), `[0,1]` (`:315`) | Input, never derived. `picard_step_encloses_trajectory` (`:620`) takes `r_pad ∈ sys.remainderPad` as a hypothesis. |
| `Hybrid.lean` | Mode ODEs `Ṫ = 4`, `Ṫ = -2`, `Ṫ = 20 - T`, guards, resets (`:184-226`) | Literals inside `decide +kernel` (`:253-268`). |
| `QuantumWalk.lean` | `remSmall = ±1/100` (`:1104`), unitary envelope `[-2,2]` (`:1109-1116`), `t = 157/100` | Literals; the envelope is wider than any amplitude can be. |

| `Magnetics.lean` | `goldenLiquidIpmMotor` (`ψ=180 mWb, Ld=150 µH, Lq=380 µH, p=4`, `:306-310`), triangle `(0,0),(2000,0),(0,1500)`, `ν=800` (`:313-321`), `kh=2, ke=1, f=400, B=16` (`:339`) | Literals inside `golden_femm_liquid_motor_magnetics_verified` (`:327-341`). The universal theorems (`:90-181,204-257,356-366,386-425,487-532`) are over all `Int`; no value matters. |

| `PowerElectronics.lean` | `goldenMs350Inverter` (`800 V, 15 nH, 8 A/ns, 1200 V, 500/180/40/100 ns`, `:273-289`); `ms350Fcml350kWSolarInverter` (`:445-461`); `goldenCoupledDriveTrainSpec` (`:647-676`) | Literals inside `golden_*_verified`. |
| `Thermal.lean` | none concrete in the electro-thermal section (`:395-577`) | Universal over `Int`, see §3 S5 for what it misses. |

| `DigitalTwin.lean` | `goldenMs350IpmPlantSpec` (`:322-351`), `goldenTwinState0` (`:359-370`) | Literals inside `golden_ms350_ipm_digital_twin_trajectory_verified` (`:386-406`). `slopeBetaCu := 0`, `alphaThermalUmPerK := 0` (`:332,338`): the two coupling coefficients are switched off. |
| `Photonics.lean` | `g = 157, 56, 60 mrad/µm`, `L = 5, 14, 11 µm`, gaps `200/225 nm` (`:857-879`) | Literals; no mode solver, no index, no wavelength anywhere in the CMT section (`:690-995`). |

| `QuantumMatter.lean` | `hypercubeQ3Quotient` (3:4:3), coupler table `[375000,500000,375000]` ppm (`:292-310`) | The one universal theorem (`:325`) says the synthesizer's output satisfies the synthesizer's own ratio check. |

| `apps/foc-hil/verilator/rk4_pmsm_plant.hpp` | `Ld=150 µH, Lq=380 µH, Rs=12 mΩ, ψ=0.18 Wb, p=4, Rth=0.045 K/W, Cth=120 J/K, C=45 µF` (`:27-36`) | C++ constants; no Lean theorem mentions this file or these values (see §3 S2). |
**INFERRED.** There is no theorem in the brief's scope whose statement is false for a different motor,
inverter, coupler or coolant. That is the operational meaning of "the physics is not in the proofs".
## 2. What is real, so it is not thrown out with the rest (READ)
- `Interval.mul_mem` (`RealAnalysis.lean:255`) is the four-corner product proved by case split on sign;
`sqr_mem` (`:276`) handles the zero-straddling case. `evalInterval_sound` (`:402`) is the fundamental
theorem of interval arithmetic for `RealExpr`. Division is absent (no `.div` constructor, `:314-321`),
so no interval ever contains zero in a denominator; fine, and limiting.
- `TaylorModel.mul_models` (`TaylorModel.lean:662-713`) does the truncation and the three cross terms
correctly; `evalPolyTermsInterval_mem` (`:567`) is a clean Horner-vs-interval lemma.
- `evalDualInterval_sound` (`Diff.lean:313`) and `meanValueEnclosure_sound` (`:407`) are the right
statements for a mean-value form. `symbolicDeriv_agrees_with_dual` (`:202`) and the reverse-mode
agreement theorems are universal.
- `sosCheck_sound` (`Judge/RealAnalysis.lean:943`): Putinar-form certificate with diagonal Gram, checked
by exact polynomial identity (`Poly.sub … .isZero`) and evaluated semantics `Poly.eval`. Sound.
- `checkSosLyapunov_sound` (`SosLyapunov.lean:413`): `V(0)=0`, `V ≥ ε‖x‖²`, `L_f V ≤ -γV` on a
semialgebraic domain, with `lieDerivativePoly` symbolic and tied to the AD (`:270`). `checkSosCbf_sound`
(`:501`) gives strict separation from the unsafe set plus Nagumo. `checkDaeManifold_sound` (`:672`)
gives tangency by ideal membership and a symbolic index-1 Jacobian. These are the best pages in
`Analysis/` and the only ones a control theorist would cite.
- `picard_step_encloses_trajectory` (`Flowpipe.lean:620-684`): the universal half is correct interval
arithmetic for a second-order Taylor–Lie step; `verifyPicardAPriori_encloses` (`:546`) is the right
inclusion check. What is missing is in §3 S4.
- `foc_drive_top.sv` lints clean: `verilator --lint-only -Wall foc_drive_top.sv` (Verilator 5.050)
prints no warnings. The 64-bit sign extension, anti-windup clamp and write-once latch are competent RTL.
- `apps/sdr-ft8/verilator/iq_synthesizer.hpp` is a real signal-level test: 79-symbol continuous-phase
8-FSK with Costas `{3,1,4,0,6,5,2}` at symbols 0/36/72 (`:5-9,36-49`) and a +40 dB opposite-sideband
jammer; the testbench measures IRR and symbol recovery (`sdr_ft8_tb.cpp:60-120`). It is the one place in
scope where the thing under test is exercised by a signal rather than by `decide`.
## 3. Suspicions, evidence, verdicts (ranked by embarrassment in front of my kind)
### S1. The automatic certificate synthesizer proves a claim over a domain it picked, not the one stated
*What made me suspicious.* `apps/foc-hil/FocDriveTop.obend:42` reads
`claim stator_temp_interval_cbf(lossWatt: Nat) by judge("interval@1"): 45n + lossWatt * 4n <= 180n`.
That is false at `lossWatt = 34`. Yet `foc_hil_all_accepted_and_claims_hold` (`FocHil.lean:1104`) says it holds.
*Evidence.* **READ** `AutoCert.lean:1952-1972`, `extractIntervalEnvFromHyps envVars defaultIv hyps`:
a variable with no `given` bound gets `(v, defaultIv)`; `extractIntervalObjFromSyntax` (`:1985-2028`)
calls it with `⟨0, 1⟩`. So the kernel-checked query for the FOC claim is `45 + 4x ≤ 180` on `x ∈ [0,1]`.
`extractTaylorModelQueryFromSyntax` (`:2056-2091`) does the same with `[-1/10, 1/10]`.
**READ** `FocHil.lean:978-1006`: the FOC app does not even use that path. Its private `synthExternalJudge`
tries `candDoms := [250, 30, 15, 8, 7, 1]` and takes the *first* upper bound for which `intervalCheck` passes
(`:985-991`); for `taylor-model@1` it ignores the claim body entirely and substitutes the fixed query
`cos+sin on [-1/10,1/10] ⊆ [4/5, 6/5]` (`:996-1001`); for `sos-lyapunov-cbf@1` it substitutes
`goldenSosProblem` (`:1002-1005`). The `taylor-model@1` claim it "certifies" is
`claim cordic_trig_taylor_enclosure(thetaMrad: Nat) by judge("taylor-model@1"): thetaMrad <= 1000n`
(`ClarkePark.obend:33`), which mentions no trigonometry at all.
**READ** `obligationMeaningWithJudges focAutoCertFormats obj just` (`FocHil.lean:1104-1120`) is the judge's
meaning of the *substituted* object; the theorem's docstring calls these "4 compile-time AutoCert claims".
**READ** the general path is the same machine: `Elab/Workbook.lean:511-519` falls through to
`synthesizeClaimExternalJudge` when derivation fails, which calls the `[0,1]` extractor.
*Reproduction.* I wrote `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ember-dev-obend/a43ef565-cc2f-412d-8808-6f075bdeea89/scratchpad/autocert/BoxDefault.obend`
with the same claim shape; `obend run BoxDefault.obend heatAt34` returns `181` (the claim is false at 34).
`obend check --obligations`/`obend prove --ground 1,34` answered `no-object` for a one-layer
`fix(compose(ProbeBase), seed)` knot, so I could not drive the CLI path to the certificate; the
`[0,1]` default is established from the code, not from a run. The CLI's own ground checker would have
refuted this claim at 34 had it reached the object (`Main.lean:570-590`), which is the right instinct in
the wrong tool.
*Verdict.* **Confirmed.** `synthesizeClaimExternalJudge_sound` (`AutoCert.lean:2369`) is true and
irrelevant: it proves the synthesized justification passes the check of the query the synthesizer
built. Nothing relates that query to the claim's own quantifier. This is the certificate boundary the
council warned about (§1.6 of `FABLE-COUNCIL-20261101.md`), now at the `.obend` surface.
### S2. The FOC controller and its plant are related by nothing but a 50 ms run, and the Lean "closed loop" is open
*What made me suspicious.* The brief's own question. A drive engineer wants to see `Ld`, `Rs`, `ω_e` and
the sample time in the stability theorem, and a PWM inverter between controller and motor.
*Evidence, Lean side.* **READ** `DigitalTwin.lean:189-209` `stepSampledDataDigitalTwin`: the measured
current is `runSarAdcN 4 0 st.iPhaseSenseMv 100 * 25` and the next state carries
`iPhaseSenseMv := st.iPhaseSenseMv` (`:202`). The sensor never sees `iqAmp`. With
`iPhaseSenseMv = 950 mV` the code is `9`, the "measurement" is a constant `225 A`, the error is a constant
`25 A`, and `iq` ramps `230 → 242 → 254` (`:392-393`) and would ramp forever. The golden theorem
(`:386-406`) certifies the ramp. `slopeBetaCu := 0` and `alphaThermalUmPerK := 0` (`:332,338`) zero the
electro-thermal and thermo-mechanical couplings, so `tWinding` and `hotAirGap` are constants in the
"coupled" trajectory (`:397-400`). `pCuBaseW := 7638` (`:331`) is chosen so that `7638 + 362 = 8000` lands
`T` exactly on `122000` (`FluidThermal.lean:324`). A 4-bit ADC at `25 A/code` (`:342-344`) is not a current
loop sensor. **READ** `sampled_data_current_loop_iss_contraction` (`:233-264`) is about
`x⁺ = x(1000-κ) + κ(r - δ)`: no inductance, no resistance, no back-EMF coupling, no integrator, no
saturation, no sample time; it is "a scalar affine map with gain `1-κ` contracts", plus the SAR bound.
`foc_hil_closed_loop_iss_and_thermal_safe` (`FocHil.lean:1273`) is that theorem re-exported.
*Evidence, HIL side.* **READ** `rk4_pmsm_plant.hpp:49-89`: the dq electrical equations are right
(`:66-68`), but `omega_e_rads` is never integrated (no `J`, no load torque; `electromagnetic_torque_nm`
`:138` is never called by `foc_hil_tb.cpp`), so there is no mechanical loop. The inverter is a wire: the
plant receives `vd_cmd_mv, vq_cmd_mv` as average voltages (`foc_hil_tb.cpp:174-178`); the RTL's
`fcml_duty_permille` output (`foc_drive_top.sv:178-185`) is connected to nothing. No PWM, no dead time,
no sensor delay, offset, noise or quantization (`llround(amp*1000)`, `tb:94-95`). The "6-level FCML
flying-capacitor" is one scalar with dynamics `-5·u - 800·cmd + ripple` (`plant:77-80`): a made-up linear
response to the controller's own command, where the command is `0.8 × last error` (`sv:162,176`), and the
test asserts the resulting decay (`tb:213,226`). Thermal: at `id=-100, iq=250` the copper loss is
winding moves **0.44 K** (`plant:82-87,27,33-35`); the 155 °C trip is *assigned* (`tb:120-124`). The
over-temperature test tests a comparator and a latch, which is fine, and should say so. RK4 at 100 ns on
a system whose fastest time constant is `Ld/Rs = 12.5 ms` is 500× oversampled and, with constant `ω` and
ZOH voltages, the plant between ticks is LTI with a closed form; RK4 validates nothing.
*Three controllers.* **READ** integral gains: `PiCurrentLoop.obend:25,45` `50/65`; Lean
`focHilSequentialRtlModule` `65` for both axes (`FocHil.lean:1447,1457`); hand-written SV `20/25`
(`foc_drive_top.sv:79-80`). The LEC (`foc_drive_lec.smt2`) compares two hand-written SMT restatements
(`spec_*` `:26-55`, `rtl_*` `:58-105`) in which `vq_active = iq_err·kp + int_q` with no `/1000`, no
feed-forward, no anti-windup, no skid register, against an SV that has all four (`sv:88-129,159-164`).
Neither side is extracted from the `.sv` or from Lean; the single `assert` is a miter of the two copies.
Z3 `unsat` says the two hand copies agree.
*Verdict.* **Confirmed.** Nothing in Lean constrains the RK4 plant or the SV; nothing in the HIL exercises
an inverter or a mechanical load. "Closed-loop 20 kHz FOC + 6-level SiC FCML HIL" is a current-loop
regression test against an idealized dq plant, and the Lean twin's loop is physically open.
### S3. Units: the golden multiphysics numbers are dimensionally wrong
*What made me suspicious.* `minShaftTorqueScaled := 20000000` (`DigitalTwin.lean:349`).
*Evidence.* **READ** `evalIpmTorqueScaled m id iq = p·(ψ_mWb·iq + (Ld_µH - Lq_µH)·id·iq)`
(`Magnetics.lean:228-229`) adds a milliweber term to a microhenry term. Golden:
was chosen to pass the scaled number. `ipm_reluctance_torque_boost` (`:236`) is fine symbolically; every
golden torque is meaningless. **READ** `evalSteinmetzCoreLossMw 2 1 400 16 = 2·400·16² + 1·400²·16² =
41,164,800` "mW" (`:339`): 41 kW of core loss at `B_pk = 16 mT`, against a `50,000,000` budget, while the
saturation check in the same call uses `1650 ≤ 1850` mT. **READ** `evalSicInverterTotalLoss`
(`PowerElectronics.lean:497-499`) sums `3·I²·R_mΩ` (mW) with `k·f_kHz·V·I`; golden `600,000 + 3,200,000 ≤
4,000,000` (`:658-662`). **READ** `evalFcmlCellBlockingVoltageV 1500 6 = 250` with integer division
(`:308-309`); `ms350Fcml350kWSolarInverter.vDcBusV := 250` then checks `250 + 50 ≤ 650` (`:447-450`) and
the docstring says "233 A (350 kW)" while the spec has `mpptI := 300` (`:443,457`). **READ** the FEM
load vector: `evalElementResidual` subtracts `J·2Δ` from each node (`Magnetics.lean:630-631`); the
consistent load for a linear triangle is `J·Δ/3` per node, and the stiffness part omits `1/(4Δ)`, so the
"discrete Ampère's law" `r0+r1+r2 = -3·J·2Δ = -6JΔ` (`:648-651`) should read `-JΔ`. On the golden triangle
(`2Δ = 3·10⁶ µm²`) the two terms are mis-weighted by `24Δ ≈ 3.6·10⁷`; it is invisible only because `J = 0`
in the golden case (`:321`).
*Verdict.* **Confirmed.** None of these break a proof, because the proofs are about `Int`; they break
every sentence in `PHYSICAL.md` §4 that quotes a number.
### S4. The validated-numerics stack: what a referee would strike
*(a) Transcendental functions are polynomials by definition.* **READ** `AnalyticModel CanonicalRat`
(`TaylorModel.lean:976-981`): `expFn := expPartialSum 8`, `sinFn := sinDegree7Odd`,
`cosFn := cosDegree6Even`, `ln1pFn := ln1pDegree6Alt`, `sqrt1pFn := sqrt1pDegree5Binom`. The
"Lagrange remainder" hypotheses (`:941-970`) are discharged for these polynomials with witnesses like
`c = -x/5040` (`:991`). I checked the typed constants against the real functions: `e/120 < 1/40`,
`(15/16)·2^{3.5}/24 ≈ 0.44 < 5/8`. They are right. Nothing in the tree says so, nothing can without `ℝ`,
and nothing uses the class. The docstring "Verified Transcendental Enclosures" (`:15`) is an overclaim;
the class itself is the correct architecture (the function model enters as a hypothesis) and deserves a
Mathlib `Real.exp` instance.
*(b) The `taylor-model@1` judge has no semantics.* **READ** `taylorModelJudge.Meaning q tm :=
verifyTaylorModelCert q tm = true ∧ …` (`AutoCert.lean:791-794`) and the FOC copy (`FocHil.lean:370-374`):
the meaning *is* the checker. Compare `intervalJudge.Meaning := IntervalQuery.SemanticMeaning`

on rotations, which is why `coupledOscillatorOde` is run for one step (`:661-666`). The "elimination of the
wrapping effect" (`taylorModel_picard_sound`, `:361-384`) is on the scalar ODE `ẋ = -x`; a scalar has no
wrapping effect, that is the dependency problem.

integrator is the non-symplectic Taylor step above. Its "unitary envelope" is `[-2,2]` on each quadrature

`lindbladDephasingOde` is `ċ = -γc` (`:1040-1045`). The degree-4 "matrix Taylor PST amplitude"
`9287743200` shipped to the RTL testbench (`quantum_photonic_tb.cpp:21`, `QuantumPhotonicMatter.lean:647`)

tube" that encloses 1 (`:1656-1662`) is `sin⁶(t)` from the hypercube closed form via half-angle, not from

plus a first-order interval ODE stepper. Every word beyond that in the docstrings is to be struck.

# Sitting next to the physicist: validated numerics, multiphysics, motor drives, photonics (2026-11-03)

Slug `physics-numerics`. The persona: validated numerics (intervals, Taylor models, verified ODE
enclosures), finite-element magnetics, motor-drive and power-electronics design, with photonics and
quantum-hardware colleagues. Working tree as of 2026-11-03, not HEAD; nothing edited but this file.

Tags: **READ** (file opened, `path:line` cited), **INFERRED** (deduced from READ facts), **PROPOSED**.
Every number has the command or the arithmetic that produced it. No Lean or Rust was built. Runs:
`verilator --lint-only -Wall` on one `.sv`; `lean/.lake/build/bin/obend check|run|prove` on a scratch
module in the session scratchpad; `grep`/`wc`.

Files read in full or by theorem statement: `lean/Obend/Analysis/{RealAnalysis,TaylorModel,Flowpipe,
Hybrid,Diff,Groebner,SosLyapunov,Equitable,QuantumWalk,EqSatHypergraph}.lean`,
`lean/Obend/Judge/RealAnalysis.lean`, `lean/Obend/Elab/AutoCert.lean`, `lean/Obend/Hardware/{Magnetics,
FluidThermal,PowerElectronics,Thermal,Physics,Photonics,QuantumMatter,Analog,RF,DSP,Accelerators,
FabuBlox,TcadBridge,DigitalTwin}.lean`, `lean/Obend/Apps/{FocHil,SdrFt8,QuantumPhotonicMatter}.lean`,
`apps/foc-hil/**`, `apps/sdr-ft8/verilator/*`, `apps/quantum-photonic-matter/verilator/*_tb.cpp`,
`stdlib/physical/*.obend`, `PHYSICAL.md` (30,403 lines by `wc -l` over the list in the brief).

---

## 0. Verdict

**READ/INFERRED.** The arithmetic core is now genuinely verified and the council's "zero theorems in
`RealAnalysis.lean`" finding is obsolete in the working tree: `Interval.add_mem/sub_mem/mul_mem/sqr_mem`,
`evalInterval_sound`, three `#tooth` probes (`RealAnalysis.lean:184-307,402-464,471-499`), the Taylor-model
algebra (`TaylorModel.add_models/sub_models/scale_models/mul_models`, `evalTaylorModelRange_encloses`,
`TaylorModel.lean:451-713`), forward-mode interval AD (`Diff.lean:313`), the SOS/Positivstellensatz
family (`Judge/RealAnalysis.lean:943`, `SosLyapunov.lean:413,501,672`) and the interval judge
(`Judge/RealAnalysis.lean:83-119`) are universally quantified over `ℚ` and their proofs are structural.
A numerical analyst would sign those pages.

Everything that *names a device* sits on top of that core without touching it. Physical constants enter
as integer literals inside `def golden…` records and `decide +kernel` theorems; no theorem has a device
parameter as a free variable whose *value* matters, and in the two places a model enters as a hypothesis
(`AnalyticModel`, `TaylorModel.lean:935`; `perturbative_disorder_leakage_bound`, `QuantumMatter.lean:1786`)
the only instance is a polynomial or the hypothesis is the conclusion's own recurrence. The FOC
"closed loop" is open in Lean (the sensor is never updated) and plant-free in the HIL (no inverter, no
mechanics, thermal state moves 0.4 K in the whole run). The automatic certificate synthesizer certifies a
claim over a domain it chose, not the domain the claim states. Three of the four golden "multiphysics"
numbers are unit mismatches a motor-drive engineer would catch in the first minute.

The referee's one-line summary: *correct interval arithmetic over the rationals, wearing the names of
machines it has never been connected to.*

---

## 1. Where does any physical constant or device parameter enter a theorem?

I asked this first of every module. The table is exhaustive for the files in the brief.

### S4. The validated-numerics stack: what a referee would strike

*(a) Transcendental functions are polynomials by definition.* **READ** `AnalyticModel CanonicalRat`
(`TaylorModel.lean:976-981`): `expFn := expPartialSum 8`, `sinFn := sinDegree7Odd`,
`cosFn := cosDegree6Even`, `ln1pFn := ln1pDegree6Alt`, `sqrt1pFn := sqrt1pDegree5Binom`. The
"Lagrange remainder" hypotheses (`:941-970`) are discharged for these polynomials with witnesses like
`c = -x/5040` (`:991`). I checked the typed constants against the real functions: `e/120 < 1/40`,
`|sin⁽⁶⁾|/720 ≤ 1/720`, `|cos⁽⁵⁾|/120 ≤ 1/120`, `32/5` for `(1+ξ)⁻⁵` on `[-1/2,1/2]`, and
`(15/16)·2^{3.5}/24 ≈ 0.44 < 5/8`. They are right. Nothing in the tree says so, nothing can without `ℝ`,
and nothing uses the class. The docstring "Verified Transcendental Enclosures" (`:15`) is an overclaim;
the class itself is the correct architecture (the function model enters as a hypothesis) and deserves a
Mathlib `Real.exp` instance.

*(b) The `taylor-model@1` judge has no semantics.* **READ** `taylorModelJudge.Meaning q tm :=
verifyTaylorModelCert q tm = true ∧ …` (`AutoCert.lean:791-794`) and the FOC copy (`FocHil.lean:370-374`):
the meaning *is* the checker. Compare `intervalJudge.Meaning := IntervalQuery.SemanticMeaning`
(`Judge/RealAnalysis.lean:75-78,110-112`), which quantifies over all rational points. The composition cases
`.exp a` etc. (`AutoCert.lean:734-758`) are plausibly sound by `evalTaylorModelRange_encloses`, and that is
exactly the theorem that is not stated.

*(c) The flowpipe proves the arithmetic half of a validated step and omits the analytic half.* **READ**
`picard_step_encloses_trajectory` (`Flowpipe.lean:620-640`): the "trajectory point" is *defined* as
`x₀ + h f(x₀) + (h²/2)(L_f f)(ξ) + r_pad` with `ξ` in the rough box (`IsPicardSegmentState`, `:569-579`).
That is the conclusion of Taylor's theorem with Lagrange remainder plus the Picard a-priori enclosure,
taken as a definition. Existence of the solution, that it lies in `X̃` on `[0,h]`, and that its value at
`h` has that form, are the content of a validated ODE step (Lohner 1987; Nedialkov–Jackson–Corliss 1999)
and are absent. `rho : String → ℚ` (`:49`), so the actual solution `20 + 10e^{-t}` of

on rotations, which is why `coupledOscillatorOde` is run for one step (`:661-666`). The "elimination of the
wrapping effect" (`taylorModel_picard_sound`, `:361-384`) is on the scalar ODE `ẋ = -x`; a scalar has no
wrapping effect, that is the dependency problem.

`lindbladDephasingOde` is `ċ = -γc` (`:1040-1045`). The degree-4 "matrix Taylor PST amplitude"
`9287743200` shipped to the RTL testbench (`quantum_photonic_tb.cpp:21`, `QuantumPhotonicMatter.lean:647`)

harmonics. `mppt_incremental_conductance_global_max` (`:113`) is the maximum-power-transfer theorem for a
*linear* source `I = I_sc - G_s V`; a PV cell is exponential, which is the whole reason the InC algorithm
exists. The FCML is "6-level" in the SV and `.obend` (`SicFcmlInverterLeg.obend:27`, `sv:2`) and "7-level,
`M = 6`" in `PowerElectronics.lean:435-437`. `statorCoupledLossHypergraph` (`EqSatHypergraph.lean:1555-1585`)
computes `T_peak = I²(w + a) + w·f - 2a + 25`; the e-graph theorem (`:1677`) is a correct equality-saturation
preservation result about an integer DAG that is not a thermal model. The five `stdlib/physical/*.obend`
objects are affine integer formulas (`gateDelayPs = fanout·8 + 20`, `transferredPowerMw = p·weight + dim`,
`peakWindingTemp = 50 + loss·R`): correct `.obend` demonstrations of `self`/`super`, carrying names.

pattern is uniform: not one checker in scope is checked against a model it did not define.

atoms.t: # Council Critique — Objective Bend, 2026-11-01
### Claude Fable 5.1, for the Multimodel Council (with Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-6 Astra)
Every claim is tagged. **READ** means I opened the file and the statement is what the text says
(file:line as of commit `7c699ca` plus the uncommitted working tree). **INFERRED** means a
conclusion drawn from several READ facts. **PROPOSED** means a design I am recommending. Where
I give a number, I give the command that produced it so anyone can rerun it. I modified no
Lean or Rust file.
## 0. Method
I read `COUNCIL-BRIEF-20261101.md`, then all twelve top-level documents (`AMBITION`, `THESIS`,
`DESIGN`, `PLAN`, `PHYSICAL`, `NEXT-MATHEMATICA`, `SILICON-ELABORATOR`, `METATHEORY`,
`GROUNDING`, `DEOS-CONTRACTS-CONSENSUS`, `README`, `TEST_READY`), then the Lean tree
(`lean/Obend/`, 452 files, ~162K lines by `find … | xargs wc`), the Rust host
(`hardware/rust-ffi/src/lib.rs`, `crates/obend-{ffi,gui,node,sandbox}`), the hardware
simulation directory, the test runners, the census, the teeth, and the git history. For every
subsystem the brief names I read the theorem *statements* and the definitions they quantify
over, not the docstrings. I also ran a mechanical check of whether the theorem names the
documents cite exist in the tree (§2.2).
The short version: the spine of this repository (Core4, Slot, Fold, Receipt, Lower, Leaf, Law,
Impact, the Vault hyperedge) is real, carefully proved, and worth building on. Waves 5–6
(Analysis numerics, Hardware physics/CAD/quantum, Silicon Elaborator, GUI bridge) are mostly
*tests wearing theorem clothing*, their documentation describes a system that does not exist,
and their integration into the spine is nominal. Argon's audit is accurate on every point I
could check and still understates the problem by about an order of magnitude, because Argon
audited individual theorems and the real failure is structural.
## 1. Headline verdict
1. **READ.** The kernel-adjacent layers are genuine metatheory: `Obend/Core/Term.lean` (the
open-recursive calculus with `mix`/`fix`/`prototype`/`split`), `Obend/Slot.lean`
(`Slot.read`, `read_blocked_exact`, `permanent_blocked_forever`), `Obend/Fold.lean`
(`Admission` with `step_of_reads`), `Obend/Receipt.lean` (`dated_sound` with the
`∨ Collision H` disjunct), `Obend/Lower/Proofs/{Sound,Checks,Complete}.lean`
(`lower_sound`, `lower_checks`, `lower_complete_ltyped_nat` by reducibility),
`Obend/Leaf/{Flatten,Specialize}.lean` (`flatten_sound`, `specialize_choice`,
`moved_pin_blocks`), `Obend/Law/Contract.lean` (`Narrows`, `CellContract` with
`inductive_preserves` as a *field*), `Obend/Vault/Hyperedge.lean` (`no_toctou`,
`vaultTurn_disjoint_commutes`), `Obend/Analysis/Impact.lean`. These are universally
quantified, their hypotheses are the right ones, and their proofs are structural.
2. **READ.** `Obend/Analysis/RealAnalysis.lean` — the rational interval arithmetic that
`Flowpipe`, `TaylorModel`, `Hybrid`, `Diff.DualInterval`, the `QuantumWalk` Schrödinger
flowpipes and the `real-analysis@1`/`intervalJudge` all rest on — contains **zero theorems**
(`grep -n "^theorem" Obend/Analysis/RealAnalysis.lean` is empty; a tree-wide grep for any
theorem mentioning `evalInterval`, `Interval.mul`, `Interval.add`, or `Interval.sqr` is
also empty). `evalInterval_correct`, `Interval.add_correct`, `Interval.mul_correct`,
`interval_add_sound`, `interval_mul_sound`, cited in `DESIGN.md` §6.3, `PLAN.md` WS 18,
and `METATHEORY.md` §3, do not exist. Every "validated numerics" theorem in the tree is a
`decide +kernel` on a concrete example. The validated-numerics pillar of "the next
Mathematica" is currently unverified arithmetic plus examples.
3. **READ.** Of 140 theorem/definition names cited in the design documents that I checked
mechanically, **59 do not exist anywhere in `lean/Obend/`** — not as declarations, not in
comments (§2.2 has the list and the script). `DESIGN.md` §1 describes a `Core4` term
language (`pi q A B`, `sigma`, `jElim`, `brand`, `quo`, `ind/ctor/matchE`, `slot`,
`quote/unquote`, files `Core/Syntax.lean`, `Core/Quantity.lean`, `Core/Eval.lean`,
`Judge/Accepts.lean`, `Judge/Proofs/OneChecker.lean`) that is not the term language in
`Obend/Core/Term.lean:22-58` and whose files do not exist. `DESIGN.md` §8 names twelve

a separate artifact from the code.
4. **INFERRED.** The single biggest architectural threat is not any one fake theorem. It is
that each wave lands *beside* the spine instead of *through* it, in direct violation of the
project's own rule ("Nothing lands beside; everything replaces", `AMBITION.md` §"What we
hold to"). There are now two interval arithmetics, two law languages, two flowpipes, two
OpenUSD models, at least four disjoint judge registries, two "kernels", and an "automaton"
that is the RTL module under another name. The value proposition — one `Judge`, one
`Slot`, one `Fold`, every domain a certificate producer checked by the kernel — is being
diluted by every wave that reimplements a private mini-kernel. §2.3 itemizes the
duplicates with file:line.
5. **INFERRED.** The second threat is the proof style of waves 5–6: 281 `decide +kernel`
proofs tree-wide (`grep -rn "decide +kernel" Obend | wc -l`), 37 theorems named
`golden_*`/`*_verified`, and a pattern where the universally quantified part of a
"theorem" is a one-line consequence of its hypotheses and the impressive part is a
concrete numeric instance (`6 = 6`, `tOuterJacket − tLcInSlot = 224000`,
`kernelCheckDecl stdKernelEnv 8 validIdNatDecl = true`). These are tests. They are
valuable as tests. They are being reported as theorems, in METATHEORY tables, with
"0 sorryAx" as the headline, and that reporting is what the council was convened to stop.
6. **INFERRED.** The third threat is that the "certificate" boundary — the whole point of
"a kernel that never trusts a search it did not run" — has been hollowed at the edges:
hardware certificate decoders select golden presets by a `"mode"` string
(`Obend/Hardware/Judge.lean:440,593,670,747,830`; `decodeRtlSynthCert` at :134 picks a
module by `dagOk`/`cdcOk` flags); the "cryptographic" decider receipt is
`sha256("{declName}:{format}:ok")`, which anyone can compute
(`Obend/Law/Contract.lean:290-297`); the GUI "Pop Out to Lean 4" emits
`theorem cell_N_law : True := by obend_law` (`Obend/FFI/Bridge.lean:647-658`), the server

and "Weave Certificate" is a one-leaf Merkle hash of the bytes with no proof checked

What follows is the evidence and then the blueprint.
## 2. Overall project critique
### 2.1 What is real, and why it matters (READ)
I want to be precise about what is good, because the blueprint in §4 builds on it and
because the burst documentation makes it hard to tell the solid parts from the painted ones.

150-file `Obend/Core/` directory (47K lines) is where the real metatheory lives

- **Leaf.** `flatten_sound` (`Leaf/Flatten.lean:355`) is `.get C.flatten m ≈b .get C.object

# Council Critique — Objective Bend, 2026-11-01
### Claude Fable 5.1, for the Multimodel Council (with Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-6 Astra)

Every claim is tagged. **READ** means I opened the file and the statement is what the text says
(file:line as of commit `7c699ca` plus the uncommitted working tree). **INFERRED** means a
conclusion drawn from several READ facts. **PROPOSED** means a design I am recommending. Where
I give a number, I give the command that produced it so anyone can rerun it. I modified no
Lean or Rust file.

---

## 0. Method

I read `COUNCIL-BRIEF-20261101.md`, then all twelve top-level documents (`AMBITION`, `THESIS`,
`DESIGN`, `PLAN`, `PHYSICAL`, `NEXT-MATHEMATICA`, `SILICON-ELABORATOR`, `METATHEORY`,
`GROUNDING`, `DEOS-CONTRACTS-CONSENSUS`, `README`, `TEST_READY`), then the Lean tree
(`lean/Obend/`, 452 files, ~162K lines by `find … | xargs wc`), the Rust host
(`hardware/rust-ffi/src/lib.rs`, `crates/obend-{ffi,gui,node,sandbox}`), the hardware
simulation directory, the test runners, the census, the teeth, and the git history. For every
subsystem the brief names I read the theorem *statements* and the definitions they quantify
over, not the docstrings. I also ran a mechanical check of whether the theorem names the
documents cite exist in the tree (§2.2).

The short version: the spine of this repository (Core4, Slot, Fold, Receipt, Lower, Leaf, Law,
Impact, the Vault hyperedge) is real, carefully proved, and worth building on. Waves 5–6
(Analysis numerics, Hardware physics/CAD/quantum, Silicon Elaborator, GUI bridge) are mostly
*tests wearing theorem clothing*, their documentation describes a system that does not exist,

## 1. Headline verdict

1. **READ.** The kernel-adjacent layers are genuine metatheory: `Obend/Core/Term.lean` (the
   open-recursive calculus with `mix`/`fix`/`prototype`/`split`), `Obend/Slot.lean`
   (`Slot.read`, `read_blocked_exact`, `permanent_blocked_forever`), `Obend/Fold.lean`
   (`Admission` with `step_of_reads`), `Obend/Receipt.lean` (`dated_sound` with the
   `∨ Collision H` disjunct), `Obend/Lower/Proofs/{Sound,Checks,Complete}.lean`
   (`lower_sound`, `lower_checks`, `lower_complete_ltyped_nat` by reducibility),
   `Obend/Leaf/{Flatten,Specialize}.lean` (`flatten_sound`, `specialize_choice`,
   `moved_pin_blocks`), `Obend/Law/Contract.lean` (`Narrows`, `CellContract` with
   `inductive_preserves` as a *field*), `Obend/Vault/Hyperedge.lean` (`no_toctou`,
   `vaultTurn_disjoint_commutes`), `Obend/Analysis/Impact.lean`. These are universally
   quantified, their hypotheses are the right ones, and their proofs are structural.

2. **READ.** `Obend/Analysis/RealAnalysis.lean` — the rational interval arithmetic that
   `Flowpipe`, `TaylorModel`, `Hybrid`, `Diff.DualInterval`, the `QuantumWalk` Schrödinger
   flowpipes and the `real-analysis@1`/`intervalJudge` all rest on — contains **zero theorems**
   (`grep -n "^theorem" Obend/Analysis/RealAnalysis.lean` is empty; a tree-wide grep for any
   theorem mentioning `evalInterval`, `Interval.mul`, `Interval.add`, or `Interval.sqr` is
   also empty). `evalInterval_correct`, `Interval.add_correct`, `Interval.mul_correct`,
   `interval_add_sound`, `interval_mul_sound`, cited in `DESIGN.md` §6.3, `PLAN.md` WS 18,
   and `METATHEORY.md` §3, do not exist. Every "validated numerics" theorem in the tree is a
   `decide +kernel` on a concrete example. The validated-numerics pillar of "the next
   Mathematica" is currently unverified arithmetic plus examples.

3. **READ.** Of 140 theorem/definition names cited in the design documents that I checked
   mechanically, **59 do not exist anywhere in `lean/Obend/`** — not as declarations, not in
   comments (§2.2 has the list and the script). `DESIGN.md` §1 describes a `Core4` term
   language (`pi q A B`, `sigma`, `jElim`, `brand`, `quo`, `ind/ctor/matchE`, `slot`,
   `quote/unquote`, files `Core/Syntax.lean`, `Core/Quantity.lean`, `Core/Eval.lean`,
   `Judge/Accepts.lean`, `Judge/Proofs/OneChecker.lean`) that is not the term language in
   `Obend/Core/Term.lean:22-58` and whose files do not exist. `DESIGN.md` §8 names twelve
   `Obend/Hardware/` modules (`RTL`, `Sim`, `Verify`, `Verilog`, `TechMap`, `STA`, `Place`,
   `Route`, `PDK`, `GDSII`, `Multiphysics`, `MixedSignal`); **none exist**. The documents are
   a separate artifact from the code.

4. **INFERRED.** The single biggest architectural threat is not any one fake theorem. It is
   that each wave lands *beside* the spine instead of *through* it, in direct violation of the
   project's own rule ("Nothing lands beside; everything replaces", `AMBITION.md` §"What we
   hold to"). There are now two interval arithmetics, two law languages, two flowpipes, two
   OpenUSD models, at least four disjoint judge registries, two "kernels", and an "automaton"
   that is the RTL module under another name. The value proposition — one `Judge`, one
   `Slot`, one `Fold`, every domain a certificate producer checked by the kernel — is being
   diluted by every wave that reimplements a private mini-kernel. §2.3 itemizes the
   duplicates with file:line.

5. **INFERRED.** The second threat is the proof style of waves 5–6: 281 `decide +kernel`
   proofs tree-wide (`grep -rn "decide +kernel" Obend | wc -l`), 37 theorems named
   `golden_*`/`*_verified`, and a pattern where the universally quantified part of a
   "theorem" is a one-line consequence of its hypotheses and the impressive part is a
   concrete numeric instance (`6 = 6`, `tOuterJacket − tLcInSlot = 224000`,
   `kernelCheckDecl stdKernelEnv 8 validIdNatDecl = true`). These are tests. They are
   valuable as tests. They are being reported as theorems, in METATHEORY tables, with
   "0 sorryAx" as the headline, and that reporting is what the council was convened to stop.

6. **INFERRED.** The third threat is that the "certificate" boundary — the whole point of
   "a kernel that never trusts a search it did not run" — has been hollowed at the edges:
   hardware certificate decoders select golden presets by a `"mode"` string
   (`Obend/Hardware/Judge.lean:440,593,670,747,830`; `decodeRtlSynthCert` at :134 picks a
   module by `dagOk`/`cdcOk` flags); the "cryptographic" decider receipt is
   `sha256("{declName}:{format}:ok")`, which anyone can compute
   (`Obend/Law/Contract.lean:290-297`); the GUI "Pop Out to Lean 4" emits
   `theorem cell_N_law : True := by obend_law` (`Obend/FFI/Bridge.lean:647-658`), the server
   redefines `obend_law` as `first | decide +kernel | decide | omega | trivial` and declares
   success when stdout lacks the substring `error:` (`crates/obend-gui/src/server.rs:3920-3985`),
   and "Weave Certificate" is a one-leaf Merkle hash of the bytes with no proof checked
   (`Bridge.lean:661-676`). The view-affordance endpoint derives the law-dial mode from
   `hash % 3` (`Bridge.lean:~640`). A stranger who clicks these buttons is being shown a
   receipt for nothing.

What follows is the evidence and then the blueprint.

## 2. Overall project critique

### 2.1 What is real, and why it matters (READ)

I want to be precise about what is good, because the blueprint in §4 builds on it and
because the burst documentation makes it hard to tell the solid parts from the painted ones.

- **Core4 as it actually is.** `Obend/Core/Term.lean:22-58`: `hole n σ`, `bound`, `lam`,
  `app`, `mix`, `fix`, `specification`, `prototype`, `reflect`, `metadata`, `project`,
  `nat`, `boolean`, `label`, `binary`, `extend`, `record`, `get`, `ifZero`, `inject`, `case`,
  `ifBool`, `perform`, `done`, `split`. Quantities are `erased | affine | linear |
  unrestricted` on arrow types (`Obend/Core/Ty.lean:8-9,314-317`). This is the minidregg
  Core4 of `GROUNDING.md` §2 plus `hole` (CMTT closures) and `split`. It is a good calculus
  for the thesis: lazy open recursion, contextual holes, a consuming destructor. The
  150-file `Obend/Core/` directory (47K lines) is where the real metatheory lives
  (adequacy, subject reduction, conservation, bidirectional completeness, equi-recursive
  rows, filtered streams, splice). I did not audit it line by line; its theorem statements
  are universally quantified and its provenance (minidregg, nanodregg) is traceable.

- **Slot / Fold / Receipt.** `Obend/Slot.lean:37-60` defines a slot as `supports : Cand →
  List Fact` and `judge : Cand → Bool`; `read_blocked_exact` says a blocked read names
  exactly the dead supports. `Obend/Fold.lean:35-48` is a small, honest abstraction:
  `Admission` with `step_of_reads` (a non-moving row's step depends only on the facts it
  reads). `Obend/Receipt.lean:459-479` `dated_sound` has the exact shape the AMBITION
  promises: either the receipt's verdict and post-state are what re-execution gives, *or*
  you have exhibited a collision in `H`. This is the correct way to state hash-dependent
  soundness without axioms.

- **Lower.** `Obend/Lower/Fragment.lean:199-330` is a real reader of Lean kernel `Expr`
  into `LExpr` (`Obend/Lower/Syntax.lean:52-76`): `Nat`/`Bool` recursors, fragment
  inductives via their recursors, structures via `split`, recursion through `f.eq_def` into
  `recConst`, specialization of type arguments at use. `lower_sound`
  (`Proofs/Sound.lean:281`) is by simulation with an `AheadChain`; `lower_checks`
  (`Proofs/Checks.lean:378`) goes through `annotated_complete`; `lower_complete_ltyped_nat`
  (`Proofs/Complete.lean:865`) is a reducibility argument. This is the best-engineered
  bridge in the repo and the one the Silicon Elaborator should actually run through (§3.3,
  §4 P7).

- **Leaf.** `flatten_sound` (`Leaf/Flatten.lean:355`) is `.get C.flatten m ≈b .get C.object
  m` under `C.closedB`, via `BEquiv`; `specSlot` (`Leaf/Specialize.lean:99`) is literally a
  `Slot LeafPin Candidate` with `supports := Candidate.supports`, and `moved_pin_blocks`
  (`:147`) is `read_blocked_exact` applied. This is the project's own rule obeyed: the
  compiler's deoptimization *is* a slot read, no new mechanism.

- **Law/Contract.** `Narrows` (`Law/Contract.lean:57`) is `∀ old new req, Admits law₂ … →
  Admits law₁ …`; `CellContract` (`:72`) carries `inductive_preserves` and `step_sound` as
  *proof fields*; `cellContract_trace_sound` (`:115`) is the induction. The concrete
  contracts in `Flowpipe.lean:152`, `OpenUSD.lean:853`, `Simplex.lean:611` discharge these
  fields with real (short) Core4 evaluation proofs. This is the right design.

- **Vault/Hyperedge.** `no_toctou` (`Vault/Hyperedge.lean:307`) is exactly the PlanBinding
  theorem minidregg promised: if the read pins cover the written cells and hold in both
  stores, validity is store-independent and the post-store agrees. `vaultTurn_disjoint_commutes`
  (`:398`) is real.

- **Consensus combinatorics.** `honest_quorum_intersection` and `qc_same_view_unique`
  (`Consensus/Simplex.lean:243-291`) are correct and cleanly proved with list-filter
  counting.

- **Clearing.** `weak_duality`, `certifies_epsilon_optimal`, `judge_certifies_epsilon_optimal`
  (`Judge/Clearing.lean:240-300`) are a genuine (small) primal-dual certificate check.

- **Teeth and census.** `Obend/Tactic/Tooth.lean` is a real mutation-testing command that
  replays the stored proof's dependency closure under a mutated definition; `Obend/Census.lean`
  refuses modules in neither build tier and runs `#assert_axioms_tree`. The *mechanism* is
  excellent. Its *application* is uneven (§2.5).

- **S1 — Prophecy as ledger.** Documents written as generation prompts were promoted to

  was the cure and was dropped.
- **S2 — No checker ⇒ theorem bridges.** A Bool checker without a `check = true → P`
  theorem is a specification, not a verifier. The pattern is uniform across Equitable,
  Hardware judges, and the Contract tiers.
- **S3 — Numerics with no number.** A Mathlib-free library cannot *state* `exp x ∈ I`. The
  team chose (correctly, per the user's own modularity principle) to avoid Mathlib in tier 1,
  then wrote transcendental "enclosures" anyway. The way out is a typeclass interface for
  the analytic model with the Taylor-remainder axioms as *fields* (not axioms), instantiated
  in a leaf (§4 P1).

  certificate producer and the Vault turn is where certificates are checked. Today
  `ValidAt` evaluates Core4 laws only; no `Format` is consulted by any turn.

  mesh/step bound, which requires S3 first.

- **S7 — Objects absent from the domains** (§2.6).
- **S8 — Names over substance in the hardware stack.** `FloatInterval` has no floats;

  with `Choice` recording, `compactTape` (backward liveness), theorems `evalTape (compactTape
  (pruneTape B t)) p = evalTape t p` for `p ∈ B` and `(compactTape t).length ≤ t.length`.
  `FRepExpr → List TapeOp` by one `toTape` with `toTape_sound`. Then the Rust
  `prune_tape_for_interval` has a Lean twin and `BinaryTapeCert` carries something the kernel
  re-evaluates (`evalEvolutionCandidatePeakTemp` already does this for one metric).
- Swept volume: `sweep (tool : FRepExpr) (path : List (SE3 × SE3))` = `min` over segment
  endpoints of the transformed tool *minus* a segment-Lipschitz pad `L·‖Δ‖` where `L` comes
  from the interval gradient of `tool` (P1's `DualInterval`) and `‖Δ‖` from `Kinematics`'
  jerk-limited profile; theorem: the continuous sweep's SDF is bounded below by the
  discrete one minus the pad. `voxel_no_gouge_sound` then quantifies over *time*.
- One OpenUSD: delete `GeometryCAM.lean:849-1003`. Model `SdfLayer := List PrimSpec`,
  `PrimSpec := {path : SdfPath, opinions : List (UsdArcKind × Term)}`, and define
  `composePrim : List SdfLayer → SdfPath → Term` by folding `Term.mix` in LIVERPS strength
  order with `Term.fix … seed` for `specializes`. Then prove the table rows about `Term`:
  `liverps_local_dominates : (composePrim …).get m ≈b (upperLayer …).get m` when `m` is
  authored locally, via `flatten_sound`. `xformOp` stacks as a `List (SE3)` folded into
  the `FRepExpr` by an affine-transform constructor (`.xform M a`, with the affine-arithmetic
  enclosure lemma added to `evalFRepAffine3D_enclosesAt`).

**P6 — Hypergraphs and the compiler.**
- Functorial reverse AD: `adjoint : StrictOpenHypergraph → StrictOpenHypergraph` built by
  mapping each edge `op` to its cotangent edges (the per-op tables already in
  `compileOpticToHypergraph`) and *reversing the wavefront order* from `layerHypergraph`;
  `adjoint_sound : evalHypergraphComb (adjoint g) (fwdEnv ++ cotangentEnv) = reverse-mode
  gradient` by induction on the layering using `layerHypergraph_sound` (`:518`, real).
- Pipelining: `compileHypergraphToRtlPipelined` inserts one `RegSpec` per wavefront stage;
  theorem: the `k`-cycle register trace equals `evalLayeredStagesSync` prefix
  (`evalLayeredStagesSync_eq_evalLayeredStages` at `:440` is the lemma to lift).
- `Compiler.lean:943`: replace the `"fib"` branch by `extractTwoStateLinearRec : LeafDef →
  Option (c₀ c₁ a b : BitVec 64)` recognising `acc' = a·acc + b·prev` structurally, with
  `compileNatRec2StateSat_sound` quantified over the extracted coefficients. Fix the
  `.app (.get self m) arg` arm to bind `arg` to a fresh wire and pass it through the slot's
  input port (the multi-arg port compiler at `:1357` already has the machinery).

**P7 — The Silicon Elaborator, honestly.**
- The thesis path exists and is unused: `kernelCheckDecl : KEnv → Nat → KConstInfo → Bool`
  is a structurally recursive Lean function over the recursive inductives in
  `Lower/Inductive.lean`. Run it through `Obend.Lower.Fragment.read` (it handles recursors,
  structures, and `eq_def`), obtain `⌜kernelCheckDecl⌝ : LExpr`, and prove by `lower_sound`
  that `Evaluates (lowerT (.app ⌜kernelCheckDecl⌝ ⌜(env, fuel, decl)⌝)) (.boolean b) ↔
  kernelCheckDecl env fuel decl = b`. If `read` refuses, the refusal names the Lean construct
  to add to the fragment — that is the real Stage-1 work the roadmap described. Until that
  lands, retitle `silicon_kernel_check_sound` as `declCheck_tag_comparator_lowers` and remove
  "Silicon Lean Kernel" from `PLAN.md`.
- `kernelIsDefEq`: port Lean4Lean's skeleton — lazy δ by definitional height, η for `lam`
  and structures, proof irrelevance (`inferType` to `Sort 0`), `Nat` literal/`succ`/binop
  reduction, level normalization. Measure against real `.olean` declarations via the
  existing `fromLeanExpr` (`Inductive.lean:394`) on `Init.Prelude` and report accept/reject
  counts in METATHEORY as numbers, not adjectives.

**P8 — ReductionMachine as a machine.** Define `Tile := {rules : List Rule, inbox : Queue
Flit, credits : Nat}`, `Router` with XY dimension-order and credit counters, `Network :=
Grid Tile × Grid Router`, and `step : Network → Network`; define `simulates : Network → Book
→ Prop` as a simulation relation and prove `automaton_simulates_book` by it. DPR becomes an
instance of `specSlot`: `Candidate.tile (bitstream) (supports := env pins)`, and the DPR
theorems become `specialize_choice`/`moved_pin_blocks` instantiated — the table in
`SILICON-ELABORATOR.md` §5.3 should be *theorems named in the code*, each row one.

**P9 — Consensus as a state machine.** Honest-node transition relation over `State`
(propose at `leader`, vote once per view (`castVote_already_voted`), finalize on `2f+1`),
adversary as any message injection by nodes in `faulty`; prove `fin_cert_unique_per_height`
from `qc_same_view_unique`, prove `no_skip_and_fin` the same way, define `SlashingReceipt`
in Lean as two conflicting signed votes by the same node and prove `accountable : conflict →
∃ r : SlashingReceipt, f+1 ≤ r.signers.length`, and decode it in `obend-node` from the Lean
`Data` encoding (the `Cert.toData/ofData?` pattern at `:337-358` is already there). Make
`simplexCellContractOf f` check a `signers : List NodeId` with `Nodup` and membership in the
committee, not a count. Attach `FinalityTier` to `VaultTurn` by a theorem (`commit at tier t
→ the turn's witnesses include a cert of tier ≥ t`), not by a lattice in isolation.

**P10 — Teeth parity and theorem hygiene.**
- Rule: a `theorem` must have at least one universally quantified variable whose instance
  the proof does not compute; otherwise it is `example` or `#guard`. Move the 37
  `golden_*`/`*_verified` and the remaining concrete `decide +kernel` facts to
  `Obend/Teeth/**/Examples.lean` (tier 2). They remain valuable regression tests.
- Every universally quantified theorem in a new module ships one `#tooth`. Census emits
  `(theorems, examples, teeth)` per directory; pre-push refuses a directory whose new
  theorems have zero teeth.

**P11 — GUI/FFI truthfulness.** Pop-out must call `Obend.Lower.Reflect.reflectTerm` /
`Workbook` on the cell's actual obligation and emit a Lean file against the built oleans
(`LEAN_PATH` to `.lake/build/lib`, which `server.rs` already locates), never a `: True`
stub; weave must decode a `TransportCert`, run `transport@1` (`Lower/Judge.lean`), and store
the *receipt's* digest; affordances must come from `Vault.Law.suggestMultiField` (the
Bellman–Ford repair exists in Lean at `Vault/Law.lean` and is re-implemented in Rust at
`server.rs` — delete the Rust copy and call Lean). Until then, label the buttons "demo".

**P12 — Put the objects back.** Choose three domain examples — the LC Drives stator
(`LcDrivesStatorUsd.obend` already exists), the `MS350` phase leg, the `Q₃` photonic array —
and make the *canonical* definition the `.obend` prototype with `#law`s; use
`Workbook.#import_obend` to bring them into Lean; state the domain theorems about
`fix (compose …) seed` objects via `flatten_sound`. Measure: number of domain theorems
whose subject is a Core4 object. Today it is two files. If the number does not rise, the
"post-Mathematica objects" thesis is not being tested by the domain work at all, and the
domain work should pause.

---

## 5. On process (INFERRED)

`git log` shows 255 commits on 2026-10-31 and +326K/−72K lines over four days, every commit
authored as `ember arlynx`, with messages like `feat(ws28-ws32): Silicon Elaborator Stage
5-6, Next Mathematica II, Physical Projections, Live .obnb Workbench Server & Networked
Simplex Cluster`. The user's own operating notes forbid quick fixes, demand ground-truth
briefs, and warn that "green + self-reported done is not verification". Waves 5–6 are the
case study for all three. The structural corrections are P0 (so that prose cannot claim
what the environment does not hold), P2/P3 (so that a module *cannot* land beside the spine
because the only way to be judged is through the registry and the only way to be used by a
theorem is through a bridge lemma), and P10 (so that a `decide` on an example cannot be
counted as a theorem). With those in place, the domain work in P4–P9 can be dispatched to
agents again safely, because the gate will refuse a mirror.

What I would keep without change: everything in §2.1. What I would delete today:
`GeometryCAM.lean:849-1003`, `Hybrid.lean:346-500` (the integer judge), the Rust Bellman–Ford
copy, the `"mode"` decoders, `FloatInterval`, and every DESIGN/PLAN sentence that P0's census
flags. What I would rename today: `automaton_simulates_book`, `silicon_kernel_check_sound`,
`taylorModel_transcendental_enclosure_sound`, `lc_drives_potsdam_dyno_comparison_verified`,
`checkLawDialPreserves`, `checkDeciderReceipt`, and the thirty-odd `*_verified` theorems, to
names that say what they prove.

The spine is good enough to deserve domains that are as honest as it is.

# The decisions ledger's kind
`DECISIONS-20261031.md` names this kind (`kind: ledger`); `obend open` in `review/` keeps the
world beside it (`.obend/world.json`) and judges every write of the ledger by the laws above, which
say what its preamble requires and the law fragment can say (2026-11-04):
- Appended to, never rewritten: `appendOnly per ##`, judged at every `## ` section (a decision is
a table row inside one). A write deletes or rewrites no line of a section; it adds lines, anywhere
in it. A refusal names the section and the number of lines the write removed.
- Every theorem a decision names is one the environment has: `cited per ##`. The lines a write adds
to a section cite no backticked name that `environment:` lacks: the census's list of the library's
constants, `lean/.lake/build/census/environment.txt`, written by `lake build Obend.Census` (tier 2,
the whole tree) or `cd lean && lake env lean tests/decisions/Environment.lean` (the tier-1
library). A refusal names the names. The names already in the ledger are history and are not
judged again; `obend status DECISIONS-20261031` lists the ones the environment lacks today.
- Dated, decided by Ember, the integrator or a lane, and claiming Ember only when Ember posted it:
not sayable for this file. A section carries many decisions and a decision row carries no field
the reader knows (per-row fields are a question for Ember in the ledger, 2026-11-04);
`lean/tests/decisions/WALKTHROUGH.md` says all three for a vault with one decision per page.
To add a decision, from `review/`:
obend post DECISIONS-20261031 ROW.md --into "Taken by lanes under standing approval, 2026-11-04"
where `ROW.md` holds the table row and the quoted text is the section's heading; `--append` puts
the lines at the end of the file instead. The owner's post is the owner's write of the page,
judged: admitted, the file is rendered with the row; refused, the file is untouched and the refusal
names the section, the law, and the line or name that would pass. The whole of it, run and checked:
`lean/tests/decisions/LEDGER.md`.
